Plot a Dumbbell Chart following WJP style guidelines

Source: R/dumbbellsChart.R
wjp_dumbbells.Rd

wjp_dumbbells() takes a data frame with long-format data and returns a ggplot object with a dumbbell chart following WJP style guidelines. Dumbbell charts show the change between two points (e.g., two years) for each category, connected by a line. Values are expected on a 0-100 percentage scale.

Usage

wjp_dumbbells(
  data,
  target,
  grouping,
  cgroups,
  colors = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  labpos = NULL,
  cvec = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  bgcolor = "#ffffff",
  color = deprecated(),
  ptheme = WJP_theme(),
  label_offset = 4,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  legend_labels = NULL,
  legend_position = "top",
  legend_direction = "horizontal",
  legend_text_size = 11,
  legend_key_size = NULL,
  legend_fontface = "bold",
  legend_justification = "left",
  headers = NULL,
  header_fontface = "bold",
  header_colour = NULL,
  header_size = NULL,
  highlight_levels = NULL,
  highlight_fontface = "bold",
  highlight_colour = NULL,
  label_align = c("left", "right"),
  label_size = NULL,
  label_colour = NULL,
  breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
  expand_mult = NULL,
  axis_line = FALSE,
  axis_line_color = "#1A1A1A",
  value_axis = TRUE,
  strips = TRUE,
  strip_color = "#EBEBEB",
  grid = TRUE,
  grid_ontop = TRUE,
  value_position = c("offset", "outside"),
  value_gap = 3,
  value_size = 10,
  value_fontface = "bold",
  point_size = 4.5,
  point_stroke = 0.5,
  segment_color = "#BFBFBF",
  segment_width = 2.5,
  clip = "on",
  layout = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Data frame containing the data to plot.

target

String. Column name of the variable that supplies the values to plot.

grouping

String. Column name of the variable that supplies the categories (Y-axis labels).

cgroups

Character vector of length 2 with the two groups to compare (the start and end points of each dumbbell).

colors

String. Column name of the variable that indicates the start and end groups (the one containing the cgroups values).

labels

String. Column name of the variable containing the value labels to display. Default is NULL (no labels).

labpos

String. Column name of the variable that contains the positions for the value labels. Default is NULL (positions are computed automatically just outside each endpoint).

cvec

Vector of two colors for the start and end points. If named, names should match the cgroups values. Default is NULL (c("#2894aa", "#482d8b") is applied).

order

Named vector mapping category values to their display order (top to bottom). Default is NULL (data order).

bgcolor

String. Hex code of the background color for the alternating row strips. Default is "#ffffff".

color

Use colors instead.

ptheme

ggplot theme to apply. Default is WJP_theme().

label_offset

Numeric. Distance in percentage points between an endpoint and its automatically positioned label (value_position = "offset"). Ignored when labpos is supplied. Default is 4.

show_legend

Logical. If TRUE, displays a horizontal point legend above the chart using the cgroups values as labels. Default is TRUE.

legend_labels

Character vector of length 2 with the legend text of the start and end points. Default is NULL (the cgroups values).

legend_position

Legend position: "top" (default), "bottom", "left", "right", or c(x, y) inside the panel.

legend_direction

String. "horizontal" (default) or "vertical".

legend_text_size

Numeric. Size of the legend text, in points. Default is 11.

legend_key_size

Numeric. Size of the legend keys, in points. Default is NULL.

legend_fontface

String. Font face of the legend text. Default is "bold".

legend_justification

String. Horizontal justification of a legend above or below the chart: "left" (default), "center", or "right".

headers

String. Column name with the group of each category; a header row is drawn above each group. Default is NULL (no headers).

header_fontface

String. Font face of the headers. Default is "bold". Weight faces such as "semibold.italic" are accepted (see wjp_fonts()).

header_colour

String. Color of the headers. Default is NULL (the color of the end points).

header_size

Numeric. Size of the headers, in points. Default is NULL (the size of the category labels).

highlight_levels

Character vector of categories whose labels are highlighted (e.g., a national average). Default is NULL.

highlight_fontface

String. Font face of highlighted labels. Default is "bold".

highlight_colour

String. Color of highlighted labels. Default is NULL (the color of the headers).

label_align

String. Alignment of the category labels: "left" (default) or "right".

label_size

Numeric. Size of the category labels, in points. Default is NULL (the size of ptheme).

label_colour

String. Color of the category labels. Default is NULL ("#524F4C").

breaks

Numeric vector with the breaks of the value axis. Default is every 20 points from 0 to 100.

expand_mult

Numeric vector of length 1 or 2. Multiplicative expansion of the value axis. Default is NULL (ggplot2's default; none with a layout).

axis_line

Logical. Draw a line under the value-axis labels. Default is FALSE.

axis_line_color

String. Color of the axis line. Default is "#1A1A1A".

value_axis

Logical. Show the labels of the value axis. Default is TRUE.

strips

Logical. Draw alternating row strips. Default is TRUE.

strip_color

String. Color of the shaded strips. Default is "#EBEBEB".

grid

Logical. Draw grid lines across the value axis. Default is TRUE.

grid_ontop

Logical. Draw the grid above the points. Default is TRUE.

value_position

String. "offset" (default) or "outside". See Details.

value_gap

Numeric. Distance, in points, between the edge of a point and its label when value_position = "outside". Default is 3.

value_size

Numeric. Size of the value labels, in points. Default is 10.

value_fontface

String. Font face of the value labels. Default is "bold".

point_size

Numeric. Size of the points (ggplot2 units). Default is 4.5.

point_stroke

Numeric. Stroke of the points (ggplot2 units). Default is 0.5.

segment_color

String. Color of the connecting segment. Default is "#BFBFBF".

segment_width

Numeric. Width of the segment (ggplot2 linewidth). Default is 2.5.

clip

String. "on" (default) or "off" (labels next to 0% or 100% stay visible).

layout

A wjp_layout() with the geometry of the chart in points. Default is NULL.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The function expects long-format data with one row per grouping (category) and colors (endpoint) combination; cgroups names the two endpoint values in order (start, end). A category may have a single value (the other row missing or NA): its point and label are still drawn. When labels is supplied without labpos, labels are placed automatically just outside each endpoint and use the endpoint color. By default, a horizontal legend is built from the two cgroups values (or legend_labels) and displayed above the chart. Use order (a named vector such as c("A" = 1, "B" = 2)) to control the top-to-bottom order of the rows.

Group headers. headers names a column with the group of each category (e.g., "Gender", "Age Group"). A header row with the group name is drawn above the first category of each group, styled with header_fontface, header_colour, and header_size. Categories with an empty or missing group (such as a national average at the top) get no header.

Value labels. value_position = "offset" (default) centers each label label_offset percentage points from its endpoint, as in earlier versions. "outside" anchors each label value_gap points from the edge of its point, on the outer side of the pair.

Geometry in points. With a wjp_layout(), the label column (label_width, label_gap), the 0-100% track (track_width), the value column (value_gap, value_width), the row and header heights (row_height, header_height, header_baseline), and the margins are fixed in points, and the category labels are drawn as a text layer.

Examples

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Always load the WJP fonts
wjp_fonts()

# Percentage of people that trust their institutions, 2017 vs 2022
data4dumbbells <- WJPr::gpp %>%
  filter(country == "Atlantis", year %in% c(2017, 2022)) %>%
  select(year, q1a, q1b, q1c) %>%
  mutate(
    across(!year, \(x) as.double(unclass(x))),
    across(!year, ~ case_when(.x <= 2 ~ 1, .x <= 4 ~ 0)),
    year = as.character(year)
  ) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE) * 100)) %>%
  pivot_longer(!year, names_to = "variable", values_to = "percentage") %>%
  mutate(
    institution = case_when(
      variable == "q1a" ~ "Institution A",
      variable == "q1b" ~ "Institution B",
      variable == "q1c" ~ "Institution C"
    ),
    value_label = paste0(round(percentage, 0), "%")
  )

wjp_dumbbells(
  data4dumbbells,
  target   = "percentage",
  grouping = "institution",
  colors   = "year",
  cgroups  = c("2017", "2022"),
  labels   = "value_label",
  cvec     = c("2017" = "#2894aa", "2022" = "#482d8b"),
  show_legend = TRUE,
  label_offset = 4
)


# Report style: group headers, a single-value row, values outside the pair,
# no strips or grid, and an axis every 25% (fictional data)
perception <- data.frame(
  category = rep(c("National Average", "Male", "Female", "18-24", "25-34"), 2),
  group    = rep(c("", "Gender", "Gender", "Age Group", "Age Group"), 2),
  series   = rep(c("Perception", "Experience"), each = 5),
  value    = c(27, 29, 25, NA, 26, 61, 60, 62, 68, 59)
)
perception$text <- ifelse(is.na(perception$value), "", paste0(perception$value, "%"))

wjp_dumbbells(
  perception,
  target          = "value",
  grouping        = "category",
  colors          = "series",
  cgroups         = c("Perception", "Experience"),
  labels          = "text",
  cvec            = c("#575796", "#B200AA"),
  legend_labels   = c("General population: perception",
                      "People with a problem: experience"),
  legend_direction = "vertical",
  headers         = "group",
  header_fontface = "bold.italic",
  header_colour   = "#575796",
  label_align     = "right",
  breaks          = seq(0, 100, 25),
  axis_line       = TRUE,
  strips          = FALSE,
  grid            = FALSE,
  value_position  = "outside",
  point_size      = 3,
  point_stroke    = 0,
  segment_color   = "#E5E8E8",
  segment_width   = 3,
  clip            = "off"
)
